questions.prompt: What evasion technique can cause bulk file retrieval to generate a FileAccessed event instead of FileDownloaded?
options: Downloading files at night when logs aren't reviewed
Fetching files via SharePoint's client object model (CSOM) rather than a normal browser download
Using a VPN to hide the source IP address
questions.explanation: CSOM-based retrieval can generate FileAccessed rather than FileDownloaded, meaning detection rules watching only FileDownloaded can miss this entirely.

questions.prompt: What does the distinct User-Agent "OneDriveMpc-Transform_Zip/1.0" tell an investigator?
options: The download came from a malicious third-party tool
A folder was downloaded as a zip file, rather than an individual file via standard browser download — informative for scoping how much data left
The file was encrypted before leaving
The download was blocked by Conditional Access
questions.explanation: This specific User-Agent string distinguishes a folder/zip download from a standard file download, which matters for accurately scoping the volume of data that actually left.

questions.prompt: What threshold does the lesson cite as one well-known pattern for flagging mass SharePoint downloads?
options: Any download at all outside business hours
More than roughly 50 files downloaded by one user within a single hour
Exactly 10 files per day per user
questions.explanation: More than ~50 files in one hour by a single user is well outside normal interactive browsing behavior and is a commonly used detection threshold.

questions.prompt: Besides direct downloads, what separate exfiltration path does this lesson describe?
options: Printing documents to a local printer
External sharing — creating an anonymous or targeted sharing link, which lets data leave without any download event at all
questions.explanation: AnonymousLinkCreated and SharingSet represent a distinct exfiltration path via external sharing links — data can leave without a download event being generated at all.
